chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Sadqa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) from his father that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

One who fasts a voluntary fast has the choice [to break it] between himself and the middle of the day. When the day has passed its midpoint, the fast becomes obligatory. The view in this narration is that the first [period], if it is after midday (zawal), is for him to fast it, and it may be said that what he does in the first [period] is obligatory, and we have explained this in other places as has preceded.
ai.seo_question: When does a voluntary fast become obligatory and can no longer be broken?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani establishes the ruling for voluntary fasting (sawm al-tatawwu'), stating that the faster has the option to break their fast at any time before the middle of the day. Once the day passes its midpoint, the voluntary fast becomes obligatory and cannot be broken. The text clarifies that the period before midday is when the choice exists, and after that point, the fast is binding.
